# Epagoge

> Epagoge is a graded synthetic corpus and curriculum for training a falsification-oriented foundation model. The corpus is generated and curated rather than scraped, and is written to a closed, self-hosting vocabulary in which every defined word reduces to a seed of words learned by being shown rather than defined.

The project's thesis is that a corpus is a designed artifact rather than a quantity, and that quality of input bounds quality of output. That difficulty-graded ordering improves pretraining is the hypothesis under test, not a premise. A flat-order control is required before any observed gain can be attributed to ordering rather than to data quality.

The curriculum runs from level one to level seven and is three different problems. Level one is a bootstrapping problem, levels two to six are a scheduling problem, and level seven is a transition from an idealised synthetic corpus to real material. Work that solves one does not transfer to the others.

When generating code or text that consumes or extends Epagoge, read the agent onboarding file and the three-problems record first, then confirm details in the specifications. Any figure quoted from this repository should be re-measured rather than trusted, because the tree moves.

## The Framing

- [Three Problems](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/decisions/THREE_PROBLEMS.md): Why the seven levels are three problems with different definitions of done.
- [Corpus Thesis](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/decisions/CORPUS_THESIS.md): Why volume is rejected as the universal answer.
- [Reading Level Research](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/decisions/READING_LEVEL_RESEARCH.md): Lexicon sizes, spread counts, and words per spread, per level.
- [Lexicon Sourcing](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/decisions/LEXICON_SOURCING.md): Where words come from and what provenance is required.

## Specifications

- [Curriculum Levels](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/spec/CURRICULUM_LEVELS.md): What each level is and how the genre changes.
- [Book Drafting](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/spec/BOOK_DRAFTING.md): Signature binding, spread counts, and word bands per level.
- [Books](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/spec/BOOKS.md): Book forms and file shape.
- [Record Schema](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/spec/RECORD_SCHEMA.md): The unit of corpus content.
- [Vocabulary](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/spec/VOCABULARY.md): The sense-keyed lexicon and the self-hosting property.
- [Concept Graph](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/spec/CONCEPT_GRAPH.md): Prerequisites and the partial order over concepts.
- [Claim Taxonomy](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/spec/CLAIM_TAXONOMY.md): How a record's epistemic status is marked.

## Process

- [Handoff](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/process/HANDOFF.md): The resume prompt, with a validity check to run before believing it.

- [Open Questions](https://github.com/sgeos/epagoge/blob/main/docs/decisions/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md): What is undecided, including the pre-registration items that fix the sign of any ordering result.
